% Pattern: head/number. Inside a proof the paper writes its facts as bold heads
% numbered by a Greek letter in parentheses, in math, after a command of its
% own that is layout only, \sn for \smallskip\noindent. Each fact is a head
% with the letter as its number, and the proof after it proves it. Seen in
% the gold pilot (set X).
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 1 status=here
% want proof-1 proof - proves=theorem-1
% want head-1 statement/fact (α) status=here
% want proof-2 proof - proves=head-1
% want head-2 statement/fact (β)+ status=none
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newcommand{\sn}{\smallskip\noindent}
\begin{document}
\begin{theorem} Every regular cardinal is large. \end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
We take a club of the cardinal.

\sn
\textbf{Fact $(\alpha)$}: $\delta > \lambda$.

\begin{proof} Otherwise the club is bounded. \end{proof}

\sn
\textbf{Fact $(\beta)^+$}: The club is closed.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
